items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2161

SPONSOR: RIVERA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a
special needs assisted living program to serve persons with neurodegen-
erative diseases

 
PURPOSE:

Establishes a special needs assisted living program to serve persons
with neurodegenerative diseases

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 4655 of the public health law as it relates to
establishing a special needs assisted living program. This section adds
a new subdivision 7, which states the guidelines for a special needs
assisted living program, which will serve people with neurodegenerative
disease such as dementia and Parkinson's disease.  This section also
states the characteristics of those that would be eligible for the
program, which includes being declined admission or readmission by a
nursing home. Within the bill, the commissioner is required to report
every two years to the legislature on the progress of the program as
well as allowing the commissioner to submit appropriate applications for
federal Medicaid reimbursement for services of the program.

Section 2 gives the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would establish a special needs assisted living program,
creating a demonstration residential program that provides medical,
nursing, and social support to persons with severe cognitive and behav-
ioral dysfunction and which will demonstrate the ability to improve
health care outcomes through palliative care and the coordination of
health care services.

The program will operate through 10 sites that are family-style resi-
dences with no more than 10 residents each, plus an additional two
persons participating in adult daycare. Each site must possess a certif-
icate of operation and maintain all resident rights and standards of
quality and performance as an Adult Care Facility under Title 2 of Arti-
cle 7 of the Social Services Law. Each resident will be cared for by
medical and nursing professionals under physician supervision and have
entered into a memorandum of understanding with regional hospitals and
nursing homes in the event a transfer is required. This demonstration
program is authorized for four years.

The success of the program will be measured by annual reports by the
Commissioner of Health. Six months before the expiration of the demon-
stration, the commissioner shall report to the legislature to recommend
possible continuation of the demonstration or to make the program perma-
nent.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-2022: S4546/A4656 Gottfried
 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2161A

SPONSOR: RIVERA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a
special needs assisted living program to serve persons with neurodegen-
erative diseases

 
PURPOSE:

Establishes a neurodegenerative with behaviors enhanced special needs
assisted living residence program to serve persons with neurodegenera-
tive diseases (such as Alzheimer's dementia, Lewy body dementia, fronto-
temporal dementia, and Parkinson's disease).

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends section 4655 of the Public Health Law as it relates to
establishing a neurodegenerative with behaviors enhanced special needs
assisted living program to serve residents of certified assisted living
residences with neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's demen-
tia, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal dementia, and Parkinson's
disease. The bill would establish guidelines for the operation of the
programs. The programs would be limited to no more than ten sites each
with no more than ten residential beds and in addition may include two
respite beds. No more than five residents per site upon admission may be
in need of twenty-four-hour skilled nursing care or medical care which
would otherwise require placement in a hospital or nursing home. Each
program will have physician oversight and supervision under contract
with the site and provide nursing services directly or under contract.
This section also states that eligibility for the program requires that
in order to be admitted the patient must have been declined admission or
readmission by a nursing home, assisted living residence, enhanced
assisted living residence, or special needs assisted living residence.
However, an admission may be requested by a lawful representative of the
resident. In all cases, a physician or nurse practitioner must certify
that the prospective resident can be safely cared for in the program.

Within the bill, a number of requirements are laid out including: to
participate in the program, assisted living operators shall obtain
certification as both enhanced assisted living residence and special
needs assisted living residence; staffing requirements and privileges;
and allows for the department to establish standards for the program.

Section 2 gives the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would establish a neurodegenerative with behaviors enhanced
special needs assisted living program to serve residents of certified
assisted living residences with neurodegenerative diseases, such as
Alzheimer's dementia, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal dementia, and
Parkinson's disease.

This innovative program of long term care would provide skilled care to
disabled individuals in a residential home environment. These individ-
uals have complex care needs and require intensive staff time in situ-
ations where neither assisted living facilities nor nursing homes are
well suited to provide care. The program is intended to fill a gap in
the continuum of long term care services being provided to residents of
the state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2022: S4546-B (Rivera) - Reported to Finance

2021: S4546-A (Rivera) - Referred to Health

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None noted.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Establishes a special needs assisted living program to serve residents of certified assisted living residences with neurodegenerative diseases, such as dementia or Parkinson's disease, who are experiencing behavior disturbances.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 100
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2161-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing
      a special needs assisted living  program  to  serve  persons  with
      neurodegenerative diseases"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  require  the  Department  of  Health to establish a
special needs assisted living program  (SNALP)  to  serve  persons  with
neurodegenerative  diseases.  To  be  eligible for the SNALP, a resident
must require 24-hour care due to a neurodegenerative disease.
 
  If signed into law, this bill would potentially  violate  the  Federal
Home  and  Community-Based Services (HCBS) Settings Rule. Doing so would
place New York at financial risk of losing funding for the HCBS program,
thereby hampering our ability to provide care to individuals who need it
most.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
